channel.title: otohay blog
channel.description: An independent, personal journal of hard questions about society. Education and opinion, not therapy or advice.

item.title: Why I think everyone should try therapy
item.description: A video script: why I think everyone should try therapy at least once, what surprised me in school, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: Why so many of us feel lonely
item.description: A video script: what the Surgeon General's report on loneliness found, what couples therapy says about needing people, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: What fights are really asking
item.description: A video script on Emotionally Focused Therapy: why many fights are a protest, the negative cycle, what's under the anger, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: Who was your secure base? What attachment theory taught me
item.description: A video script on attachment theory: Bowlby's report, Ainsworth's Strange Situation, the love quiz, earned security, the feminist critique, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: Why mental health matters
item.description: A video script: half of mental health conditions start by age 14, many people wait years for help, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: Learning how to apologize, and how to move on
item.description: A video script on repair: what couples research and restorative justice taught me about apologizing, guilt versus shame, and letting myself move on.

item.title: Why we blame the person instead of the situation
item.description: A video script on the fundamental attribution error: the Castro essays, the Good Samaritan study, how culture shapes blame, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: How competition wears down the people at the bottom
item.description: A video script: survival of the fittest, Adam Smith's sympathy, the Matthew effect, the Whitehall study, mutual aid, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: Why therapists learn cultural humility
item.description: A video script with some history: the Tuskegee study, cultural competence, two doctors in Oakland who offered the word humility, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: Socialism starts with culture: Philadelphia
item.description: A video script: why I think neighbors practice sharing before a country votes for it, Gramsci's war of position, and what Philly has shared since 1731.

item.title: Who raises a kid? Bronfenbrenner's circles
item.description: A video script on Urie Bronfenbrenner's map of everything that raises a kid, what it changed about how I think about blame, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: The person is not the problem: what narrative therapy taught me
item.description: A video script on Michael White and David Epston's narrative therapy, how it changed the way I talk about homelessness, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: The identified patient: what one struggling kid can be carrying
item.description: A video script on the family therapy idea of the identified patient, where I see it outside the therapy room, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: Who gets to be called a thinker? Gramsci and Collins
item.description: A short video script: Gramsci on who gets the title of thinker, Patricia Hill Collins on knowledge built outside universities, and three steps I'm trying.

item.title: My parents never had a word for it: intergenerational trauma
item.description: A video script about intergenerational trauma as a Vietnamese American: the rules of my house, why they made sense, and three things I'm trying.

item.title: Somewhere to put it: what society owes kids with nowhere to go
item.description: Why so many kids have nowhere to put their anger: who public space is for, how Bronx kids invented hip hop as their own outlet, and what we choose to pay for.

item.title: The story my family handed me
item.description: A video script telling my story in scenes: growing up Vietnamese American in Pennsylvania, moving to San Diego, a role-play in therapy school, and what's helping me.

item.title: Do you know the number for a mental health emergency?
item.description: A short video script about 988, the free and confidential crisis line most people still haven't heard of.

item.title: Where power and identity cross: intersectionality through Foucault
item.description: A student reads Kimberlé Crenshaw's intersectionality next to Michel Foucault's ideas about power, knowledge and categories. Foucault never used the word. Putting them together is my own reading.

item.title: Who Gets Measured, and Who Does the Measuring
item.description: A reading of two school debates, behavior scores and AI glasses at exams, through Michel Foucault's idea of the examination. My own reading, not his voice.

item.title: Fearless speech for regular people: parrhesia meets boundary scripts
item.description: Foucault's idea of parrhesia, what it is not, and four short boundary sentences for work and family.

item.title: The rules nobody said out loud
item.description: A student on the unspoken rules families run on: a quick test to find yours, why they made sense once, where I caught myself running mine, and three ways to spot your own.

item.title: What therapy ethics codes get right and miss about culture
item.description: A student's read of the AAMFT and CAMFT codes of ethics through a multicultural lens: where they ask for respect and awareness, and where they stop short on power, privilege and systems.

item.title: Is there a perfect income? Why happiness seems to level off
item.description: A student reads the research on money and happiness: the famous $75,000 plateau, the studies that challenged it, and why more income matters less the more you have.

item.title: Love that showed up as food: growing up in a quiet Vietnamese American home
item.description: A student's story about a home where love came through cooking and fixing things instead of words, where that came from, and what I'm still working on as a future therapist.

item.title: Privilege is everything you never had to think about
item.description: A blunt student take on privilege: the list of things that were easy that you never noticed were easy, and how to start seeing your own.

item.title: One roll of toilet paper: what a week of scarcity taught me
item.description: A student's honest look at a class assignment where one roll had to last a week: how scarcity takes up headspace, why my frugality is a choice, and what it means for the clients I want to help.

item.title: The "I Am" poem and who we say we are
item.description: A student on writing an "I Am" poem for a capstone class: where people start, why heritage lines carry so much, and why reading it out loud was the hard part.

item.title: Social privilege: we didn't all start at the same line
item.description: A student's honest take on social privilege: a privilege-walk video, the statement that caught me off guard, why effort isn't the whole story, and a short exercise to find your own line.

item.title: Social location: where you stand decides what you see
item.description: A blunt student take on social location: the stack of race, class, family and culture that decides what you notice, what you miss, and what you call normal.

item.title: What a Freudian slip can and cannot tell us
item.description: A student's look at Freud, slips of the tongue, and the unconscious: what Freud claimed, what researchers found since, and where schemas and attachment theory fit.

item.title: What Arendt meant by the banality of evil
item.description: Hannah Arendt watched Adolf Eichmann's trial and coined a phrase people still misread. What she claimed, what critics say, and why thinking matters.

item.title: Philadelphia protests and rallies, late October to early November
item.description: A sourced, plain list of public protests, rallies, and vigils in Philadelphia through November 7, with what is uncertain.

item.title: What we teach men about pain: stigma, silence, and the help that misses them
item.description: Why help so often fails to reach men: what the CDC and NIMH numbers show, what may be missed, and the rules many of us inherit.

item.title: When a label becomes the problem: power/knowledge meets diagnosis
item.description: Foucault on power, knowledge and norms: labels can help people, and it is still fair to ask who decided where the line goes.

item.title: The watcher in your pocket: the panopticon meets social media
item.description: How a prison design from 1786 explains why we edit ourselves online, and one small thing to try this week.

item.title: A President Who Understands How Systems Feel
item.description: Why I might support Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez if she runs for president in 2028: social location, her record, and a politics that connects housing, health, climate, and daily costs.

item.title: When Watching Students Becomes the Lesson
item.description: Schools collect more data on students than ever. They should have to show it helps, explain it, and let people push back when it is wrong.

item.title: A school should be a harbor
item.description: Eight small, testable ways to make a school feel safe: private help, a calm start, a quiet room, meals without shame, and rules that listen.

item.title: A Most Agreeable War
item.description: An essay in the manner of an old drawing-room novel: on the pride of the men who start wars and the prejudice of the people asked to cheer them on.

item.title: What I'm Learning About Third Parties
item.description: Most Americans say they want a third major party and almost none vote for one. A sourced explainer on why third parties lose, what they win anyway, and the reforms already changing the rules.

item.title: A Rest From Happiness
item.description: Being happy is good. Being expected to be happy all the time is work, and work needs breaks. On giving yourself permission to just be okay.

item.title: How great thinkers are made
item.description: Six habits that build a sharper mind, from reading the originals to arguing with people who disagree.
